newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity up strongly on heat, physicals.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity up strongly on heat, physicals.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures rose strongly Monday on hot weather in the U.S. West and higher physical power prices, industry sources said.
"It's hot, so that's definitely a factor, and physical prices are up this morning," said one Western power trader.

As of 1230 EDT, September Palo Verde (PV) was up $1.77 at $30.45 per megawatt hour (MWh) after exchanges in a range of $29.70-30.75, while October PV was up $1.10 at the day's high of $23.40 following trade as low as $23.00 per MWh.

September California Oregon Border (COB) was up $1.77 at $24.50 following exchanges at $23.85-24.60, while October was trading 77 cents at the day's low of $22.00 after exchanges as high as $22.10 per MWh.
NYMEX said as of 1140 EDT an estimated total of 128 PV and 83 COB contracts had traded.
In the physical market, next-day peak PV was said to have traded at $45.50, compared with $28.50-29.50 for peak Saturday/Monday delivery in Friday discussion, sources said.
Next-day COB was said to have traded at $27.00 from $19.25-21.25 on Friday for Saturday/Monday delivery.
Temperatures were expected to reach highs of 104 degrees Fahrenheit in Phoenix, Ariz., and of 97 degrees in Sacramento, Calif., with humid conditions Monday.
Separately, power output from the 1,221 megawatt (MW) Palo Verde nuclear power unit 3 in Wintersburg, Ariz., was reduced to 90 percent of capacity as of early Monday for repairs to a condensate pump.
The unit was expected to return to full power within the next 48 hours, a spokesman for the plant said.
The adjacent 1,221 MW Palo Verde nuclear power unit 2 was operating at 93 percent of capacity as of early Monday as the unit coasts down to a scheduled refueling outage September 6.
Also, turbines totaling 1,425 MW of power capacity were off line at the massive Grand Coulee Dam in Washington state, but one 600 MW unit at the project was scheduled to restart Friday.
Separately, the 750 MW unit 5 at the Four Corners coal-fired power complex in New Mexico was expected to restart Sunday after being shut earlier this month for repairs.
The 254 MW unit 1 at the Valmy coal-fired power plant in Nevada was expected to restart Sunday or Monday after being shut earlier this week due to a rotor problem.
In the Pacific Northwest, temperatures were expected to be about four degrees Fahrenheit above normal in the northwest and near normal in the southeast through the week, Weather Services Corp said.
In the Southwest, temperatures were expected to average two to four degrees below normal in the extreme east, near normal in the central sections and four to five degrees above normal in the west.
Transmission capacity on the Pacific Intertie, which links the Pacific Northwest to Southern Califoria, remained at 6,300 MW pending final approval of system operating procedures.
Once those are cleared, which is expected by Monday, the rating will be lifted to 6,900 MW.
